tagline: Around a desert range with peaks named for racers.
intro: Off Interstate 80 at Exit 4 near Wendover, the byway heads toward Leppy Pass and then goes all the way around the Silver Island Mountains, a 54-mile loop with the Bonneville Salt Flats under the southeast flank and the Pilot Valley Playa to the west. The old shorelines of Lake Bonneville are cut into the slopes as terraces.

The Donner-Reed party passed north of the range in 1846 on the Hastings Cutoff, and Donner Canyon keeps their name. The peaks went to faster travelers. Tetzlaff Peak and Graham Peak are named for drivers who raced on the salt below.

moments.title: Tetzlaff Peak
moments.text: The peak rises 2,000 feet out of the salt flats in a single mile and is named for Teddy Tetzlaff, who drove a Blitzen Benz 142.8 miles per hour on the flats in 1914.

moments.title: California Trail
moments.text: Along the north end of the loop the byway runs with the old California Trail, and wagon wheel ruts are still pressed into the ground.

moments.title: Volcano Peak
moments.text: Near the close of the loop Volcano Peak stands 1,800 feet above the salt flats, with Wendover six miles off to the southwest.

sources.label: BLM, Silver Island Mountain Back Country Byway
